note: Proposed corrections to the Hebrew–English readings from the 9 November 2026 full reading of the 39 books, each confirmed on a second reading. Nothing here has been applied to the staging site or to the book folders. proposed_english is the full reading with the correction made.

corrections.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר יִצְחָק אֶל־אַבְרָהָם אָבִיו וַיֹּאמֶר אָבִי וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֶּנִּי בְנִי וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּה הָאֵשׁ וְהָעֵצִים וְאַיֵּה הַשֶּׂה לְעֹלָה׃
corrections.english: Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father!” He answered, “Here I am, my son.” Isaac said, “Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the animal for the burnt offering?”

first_reading.proposed: Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father!” He answered, “Here I am, my son.” Isaac said, “Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”
first_reading.reason: הַשֶּׂה (ha-seh) is specifically a sheep or lamb, one of the flock; 'the animal' is generic and loses the word's sense.

second_reading.note: הַשֶּׂה is a head of the flock (sheep or goat), not any animal; 'the animal' under-translates the word, and 'sheep' restores its sense.

corrections.proposed_english: Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father!” He answered, “Here I am, my son.” Isaac said, “Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”

corrections.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְרָהָם אֱלֹהִים יִרְאֶה־לּוֹ הַשֶּׂה לְעֹלָה בְּנִי וַיֵּלְכוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם יַחְדָּו׃
corrections.english: Abraham said, “God will provide for Himself the animal for the burnt offering, my son.” The two went together.

first_reading.proposed: Abraham said, “God will provide for Himself the sheep for the burnt offering, my son.” The two went together.
first_reading.reason: הַשֶּׂה (ha-seh) is specifically a sheep or lamb, one of the flock; 'the animal' is generic and loses the word's sense.

second_reading.note: הַשֶּׂה is a head of the flock (sheep or goat), not any animal; 'the animal' under-translates the word, as in 22:7.

corrections.proposed_english: Abraham said, “God will provide for Himself the sheep for the burnt offering, my son.” The two went together.

corrections.hebrew: וַתְּמַהֵר וַתּוֹרֶד כַּדָּהּ מֵעָלֶיהָ וַתֹּאמֶר שְׁתֵה וְגַם־גְּמַלֶּיךָ אַשְׁקֶה וָאֵשְׁתְּ וְגַם הַגְּמַלִּים הִשְׁקָתָה׃
corrections.english: “And she quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels.’ So I drank, and she watered my camels.”

first_reading.proposed: “And she quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I will also water your camels.’ So I drank, and she watered the camels also.”
first_reading.reason: וְגַם־גְּמַלֶּיךָ אַשְׁקֶה and וְגַם הַגְּמַלִּים הִשְׁקָתָה: וְגַם 'also' (the point of the sign, kept in 24:14) is dropped twice, and הַגְּמַלִּים 'the camels' becomes 'my camels'.

second_reading.note: וְגַם stands before both גְּמַלֶּיךָ אַשְׁקֶה and הַגְּמַלִּים הִשְׁקָתָה and is dropped twice; הַגְּמַלִּים is 'the camels', not 'my camels'.

corrections.proposed_english: “And she quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I will also water your camels.’ So I drank, and she watered the camels also.”

corrections.hebrew: וְרִבְקָה שֹׁמַעַת בְּדַבֵּר יִצְחָק אֶל־עֵשָׂו בְּנוֹ וַיֵּלֶךְ עֵשָׂו הַשָּׂדֶה לָצוּד צַיִד לְהָבִיא׃
corrections.english: Now Rebekah heard Isaac speaking to Esau, his son; and Esau went out into the plain to hunt game and bring it.

first_reading.proposed: Now Rebekah heard Isaac speaking to Esau, his son; and Esau went out into the field to hunt game and bring it.
first_reading.reason: הַשָּׂדֶה is 'the field' (open country), rendered 'field' in 27:3 for the same word; 'plain' is not its sense and echoes the Greek column's wording.

second_reading.note: הַשָּׂדֶה is the field or open country where game is hunted (so 27:3); 'plain' is a topographic sense the word does not carry.

corrections.proposed_english: Now Rebekah heard Isaac speaking to Esau, his son; and Esau went out into the field to hunt game and bring it.

corrections.hebrew: עַל־כֵּן לֹא־יֹאכְלוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה אֲשֶׁר עַל־כַּף הַיָּרֵךְ עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה כִּי נָגַע בְּכַף־יֶרֶךְ יַעֲקֹב בְּגִיד הַנָּשֶׁה׃
corrections.english: Therefore the Israelites do not eat the sinew at the hip socket to this day, because he touched Jacob’s hip socket at that sinew.

first_reading.proposed: Therefore the Israelites do not eat the sinew of the thigh that is at the hip socket to this day, because he touched Jacob’s hip socket at the sinew of the thigh.
first_reading.reason: גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה (twice) is 'the sinew of the thigh/sciatic sinew'; the English renders only גִּיד 'the sinew' and leaves הַנָּשֶׁה untranslated both times.

second_reading.note: גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה occurs twice and הַנָּשֶׁה is rendered neither time; the current English gives only גִּיד and the clause אֲשֶׁר עַל־כַּף הַיָּרֵךְ.

corrections.proposed_english: Therefore the Israelites do not eat the sinew of the thigh that is at the hip socket to this day, because he touched Jacob’s hip socket at the sinew of the thigh.

corrections.hebrew: וַיָּמָת חֻשָׁם וַיִּמְלֹךְ תַּחְתָּיו הֲדַד בֶּן־בְּדַד הַמַּכֶּה אֶת־מִדְיָן בִּשְׂדֵה מוֹאָב וְשֵׁם עִירוֹ עֲוִית׃
corrections.english: And Husham died, and Hadad, son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the plain of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith.

first_reading.proposed: And Husham died, and Hadad, son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith.
first_reading.reason: בִּשְׂדֵה מוֹאָב is 'in the field/country of Moab' (cf. שְׂדֵה אֱדוֹם rendered 'country of Edom' at 32:3); 'plain' is not the sense of שָׂדֶה and echoes the Greek column's wording.

second_reading.note: שְׂדֵה מוֹאָב is the territory or country of Moab; 'plain of Moab' is not the sense of שָׂדֶה and suggests עַרְבוֹת מוֹאָב, a different term.

corrections.proposed_english: And Husham died, and Hadad, son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith.

corrections.hebrew: וַיָּשָׁב אֶל־יְהוּדָה וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא מְצָאתִיהָ וְגַם אַנְשֵׁי הַמָּקוֹם אָמְרוּ לֹא־הָיְתָה בָזֶה קְדֵשָׁה׃
corrections.english: So he returned to Judah and said, “I did not find her; and moreover, the men of the place said, ‘There is no prostitute here.’”

first_reading.proposed: So he returned to Judah and said, “I did not find her; and moreover, the men of the place said, ‘There has been no prostitute here.’”
first_reading.reason: לֹא־הָיְתָה בָזֶה קְדֵשָׁה has perfect הָיְתָה, 'there was/has been no prostitute here' (so rendered in 38:21); the English shifts it to present 'There is no'.

second_reading.note: הָיְתָה is perfect, 'there was / has been no קְדֵשָׁה here'; present 'There is no' shifts the tense of the townsmen's report.

corrections.proposed_english: So he returned to Judah and said, “I did not find her; and moreover, the men of the place said, ‘There has been no prostitute here.’”

corrections.hebrew: וַיְהִי כְּמִשְׁלֹשׁ חֳדָשִׁים וַיֻּגַּד לִיהוּדָה לֵאמֹר זָנְתָה תָּמָר כַּלָּתֶךָ וְגַם הִנֵּה הָרָה לִזְנוּנִים וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוּדָה הוֹצִיאוּהָ וְתִשָּׂרֵף׃
corrections.english: And it came to pass after three months that it was reported to Judah, saying, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the prostitute, and behold, she is with child from prostitution.” Then Judah said, “Bring her out and let her be burned.”

first_reading.proposed: And it came to pass after about three months that it was reported to Judah, saying, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the prostitute, and behold, she is with child from prostitution.” Then Judah said, “Bring her out and let her be burned.”
first_reading.reason: כְּמִשְׁלֹשׁ חֳדָשִׁים has approximating כְּ, 'about three months'; the English gives an exact 'after three months'.

second_reading.note: כְּמִשְׁלֹשׁ חֳדָשִׁים carries approximating כְּ, 'about three months', which the current English drops; וְגַם before הִנֵּה also stays unrendered.

corrections.proposed_english: And it came to pass after about three months that it was reported to Judah, saying, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the prostitute, and behold, she is with child from prostitution.” Then Judah said, “Bring her out and let her be burned.”

corrections.hebrew: וַתָּבֹאנָה אֶל־קִרְבֶּנָה וְלֹא נוֹדַע כִּי־בָאוּ אֶל־קִרְבֶּנָה וּמַרְאֵיהֶן רַע כַּאֲשֶׁר בַּתְּחִלָּה וָאִיקָץ׃
corrections.english: “And they went into their bellies; yet it was completely imperceptible that they had gone into their bellies, for their appearance remained as ugly as at the beginning, then I awoke.”

first_reading.proposed: “And they went into their bellies; yet it was imperceptible that they had gone into their bellies, for their appearance remained as ugly as at the beginning, then I awoke.”
first_reading.reason: וְלֹא נוֹדַע is simply 'and it was not known'; the intensifier 'completely' has no counterpart in the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: וְלֹא נוֹדַע is plain 'and it was not known'; no infinitive absolute or adverb supports the added 'completely'.

corrections.proposed_english: “And they went into their bellies; yet it was imperceptible that they had gone into their bellies, for their appearance remained as ugly as at the beginning, then I awoke.”

corrections.hebrew: וְהָרָעָב הָיָה עַל כָּל־פְּנֵי הָאָרֶץ וַיִּפְתַּח יוֹסֵף אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר בָּהֶם וַיִּשְׁבֹּר לְמִצְרַיִם וַיֶּחֱזַק הָרָעָב בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
corrections.english: And the famine was upon the face of all the earth. Then Joseph opened all the granaries and sold to all the Egyptians; and the famine prevailed in the land of Egypt.

first_reading.proposed: And the famine was upon the face of all the earth. Then Joseph opened all the granaries and sold to the Egyptians; and the famine prevailed in the land of Egypt.
first_reading.reason: וַיִּשְׁבֹּר לְמִצְרַיִם is 'sold to Egypt/the Egyptians'; 'all' has no Hebrew basis and matches the Septuagint's 'to all the Egyptians' ('granaries' for כָּל־אֲשֶׁר בָּהֶם is defensible via Targum/Rashi).

second_reading.note: וַיִּשְׁבֹּר לְמִצְרַיִם has no כָּל; 'to all the Egyptians' adds a word found in the Septuagint, not in this Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: And the famine was upon the face of all the earth. Then Joseph opened all the granaries and sold to the Egyptians; and the famine prevailed in the land of Egypt.

corrections.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר פַּרְעֹה אֶל־יַעֲקֹב כַּמָּה יְמֵי שְׁנֵי חַיֶּיךָ׃
corrections.english: And Pharaoh asked Jacob, “How many are the years of the days of your life?”

first_reading.proposed: And Pharaoh asked Jacob, “How many are the days of the years of your life?”
first_reading.reason: כַּמָּה יְמֵי שְׁנֵי חַיֶּיךָ is 'the days of the years of your life'; the English inverts the construct chain to 'the years of the days'.

second_reading.note: יְמֵי שְׁנֵי חַיֶּיךָ is 'the days of the years of your life'; the current English reverses the construct chain.

corrections.proposed_english: And Pharaoh asked Jacob, “How many are the days of the years of your life?”

corrections.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה עוֹד נֶגַע אֶחָד אָבִיא עַל־פַּרְעֹה וְעַל־מִצְרַיִם אַחֲרֵי־כֵן יְשַׁלַּח אֶתְכֶם מִזֶּה כְּשַׁלְּחוֹ כָּלָה גָּרֵשׁ יְגָרֵשׁ אֶתְכֶם מִזֶּה׃
corrections.english: YHWH said to Moses, “I will bring one more plague upon Pharaoh and Egypt. Afterward he will let you go from here. When he lets you go, he will drive you out completely.

first_reading.proposed: YHWH said to Moses, “I will bring one more plague upon Pharaoh and Egypt. Afterward he will let you go from here. When he lets you go, he will drive you out from here completely.
first_reading.reason: The second מִזֶּה ("from here") in גָּרֵשׁ יְגָרֵשׁ אֶתְכֶם מִזֶּה is left untranslated; the Hebrew says he will drive you out "from here".

second_reading.note: מִזֶּה stands twice, after יְשַׁלַּח אֶתְכֶם and after גָּרֵשׁ יְגָרֵשׁ אֶתְכֶם; the second 'from here' is unrendered.

corrections.proposed_english: YHWH said to Moses, “I will bring one more plague upon Pharaoh and Egypt. Afterward he will let you go from here. When he lets you go, he will drive you out from here completely.

corrections.hebrew: וְהָיָה לְאַהֲרֹן וּלְבָנָיו לְחָק־עוֹלָם מֵאֵת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי תְרוּמָה הוּא וּתְרוּמָה יִהְיֶה מֵאֵת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל מִזִּבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵיהֶם תְּרוּמָתָם לַיהוָה׃
corrections.english: These shall belong to Aaron and his sons by a perpetual statute from the sons of Israel. It is a contribution, taken from the sacrifices of their peace offerings as their contribution to YHWH.

first_reading.proposed: These shall belong to Aaron and his sons by a perpetual statute from the sons of Israel. It is a contribution, and it shall be a contribution from the sons of Israel, taken from the sacrifices of their peace offerings as their contribution to YHWH.
first_reading.reason: The clause וּתְרוּמָה יִהְיֶה מֵאֵת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל ("and it shall be a contribution from the sons of Israel") is collapsed into "taken from"; the second statement and its "from the sons of Israel" are not rendered.

second_reading.note: The clause וּתְרוּמָה יִהְיֶה מֵאֵת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל is missing; the current English jumps from תְרוּמָה הוּא straight to מִזִּבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵיהֶם.

corrections.proposed_english: These shall belong to Aaron and his sons by a perpetual statute from the sons of Israel. It is a contribution, and it shall be a contribution from the sons of Israel, taken from the sacrifices of their peace offerings as their contribution to YHWH.

corrections.hebrew: כִּי עֲנַן יְהוָה עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּן יוֹמָם וְאֵשׁ תִּהְיֶה לַיְלָה בּוֹ לְעֵינֵי כָל־בֵּית־יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל־מַסְעֵיהֶם׃
corrections.english: For the cloud of YHWH was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was over it by night, in the sight of the whole house of Israel throughout all their journeys.

first_reading.proposed: For the cloud of YHWH was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of the whole house of Israel throughout all their journeys.
first_reading.reason: וְאֵשׁ תִּהְיֶה לַיְלָה בּוֹ: bo means 'in it' (the fire was in the cloud), not 'over it'; the English repeats the preposition of עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּן from the first clause.

second_reading.note: בּוֹ means 'in it', not 'over it'; the current English carries עַל from עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּן into the second clause.

corrections.proposed_english: For the cloud of YHWH was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of the whole house of Israel throughout all their journeys.

corrections.hebrew: וְרָאָה הַכֹּהֵן אַחֲרֵי הֻכַּבֵּס אֶת־הַנֶּגַע וְהִנֵּה לֹא־הָפַךְ הַנֶּגַע אֶת־עֵינוֹ וְהַנֶּגַע לֹא־פָשָׂה טָמֵא הוּא בָּאֵשׁ תִּשְׂרְפֶנּוּ פְּחֶתֶת הִוא בְּקָרַחְתּוֹ אוֹ בְגַבַּחְתּוֹ׃
corrections.english: After it has been washed, the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has not changed its appearance, though it has not spread, it is unclean. Burn it with fire; it is a corrosive condition on its bare side or its hairy side.

first_reading.proposed: After it has been washed, the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has not changed its appearance, though it has not spread, it is unclean. Burn it with fire; it is a corrosive condition on its back side or its front side.
first_reading.reason: בְגַבַּחְתּוֹ is 'its frontal baldness', the bare spot on the front/outer side (paired with בְקָרַחְתּוֹ, back/inner side); neither word means 'hairy'. The contrast is back versus front, not bare versus hairy.

second_reading.note: גַּבַּחְתּוֹ is frontal baldness, the opposite of 'hairy'; paired with קָרַחְתּוֹ it marks the fabric's front against its back.

corrections.proposed_english: After it has been washed, the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has not changed its appearance, though it has not spread, it is unclean. Burn it with fire; it is a corrosive condition on its back side or its front side.

corrections.hebrew: וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִים בָּכֶם יִמַּקּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָם בְּאַרְצֹת אֹיְבֵיכֶם וְאַף בַּעֲוֺנֹת אֲבֹתָם אִתָּם יִמָּקּוּ׃
corrections.english: Those of you who remain shall waste away in their guilt in their enemies’ lands; also in the guilt of their fathers they shall waste away with them.

first_reading.proposed: Those of you who remain shall waste away in their guilt in your enemies’ lands; also in the guilt of their fathers they shall waste away with them.
first_reading.reason: בְּאַרְצֹת אֹיְבֵיכֶם has a second-person plural suffix, 'your enemies' lands'; the English gives 'their enemies' lands' (the Septuagint's third person).

second_reading.note: אֹיְבֵיכֶם has the second-person plural suffix, 'your enemies'; 'their enemies' is the wrong person, though בַּעֲוֺנָם is rightly 'their'.

corrections.proposed_english: Those of you who remain shall waste away in their guilt in your enemies’ lands; also in the guilt of their fathers they shall waste away with them.

corrections.hebrew: וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה מִמַּחֲצִת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־הָאָחֻז אֶחָד מִן־הַחֲמִשִּׁים מִן־הָאָדָם וּמִן־הַבְּהֵמָה וַיִּתֵּן אֹתָם לַלְוִיִּם שֹׁמְרֵי מִשְׁמֶרֶת מִשְׁכַּן יְהוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהוָה אֶת־מֹשֶׁה׃

second_reading.note: מִמַּחֲצִת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל stands in this verse and is not rendered; without it the verse does not say which half Moses drew from.

corrections.proposed_english: Moses took from the Israelites’ half one out of every fifty, from the people and livestock, and gave them to the Levites who kept the charge of YHWH’s tabernacle, as YHWH had commanded Moses.

corrections.hebrew: וְזָכַרְתָּ כִּי־עֶבֶד הָיִיתָ בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם וַיֹּצִאֲךָ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִשָּׁם בְּיָד חֲזָקָה וּבִזְרֹעַ נְטוּיָה עַל־כֵּן צִוְּךָ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת־יוֹם הַשַׁבָּת׃

first_reading.reason: מִשָּׁם (mi-sham, 'from there') after וַיֹּצִאֲךָ is not rendered.

second_reading.note: מִשָּׁם follows וַיֹּצִאֲךָ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ and is left out; 'from there' restores it.

corrections.proposed_english: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and that YHWH your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore YHWH your God commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.

corrections.hebrew: וּבָתִּים מְלֵאִים כָּל־טוּב אֲשֶׁר לֹא־מִלֵּאתָ וּבֹרֹת חֲצוּבִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא־חָצַבְתָּ כְּרָמִים וְזֵיתִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא־נָטָעְתָּ וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ׃
corrections.english: houses full of good things you did not fill, hewn cisterns you did not hew, vineyards and olive groves you did not plant—and you eat and are satisfied,

first_reading.proposed: houses full of all good things you did not fill, hewn cisterns you did not hew, vineyards and olive groves you did not plant—and you eat and are satisfied,
first_reading.reason: כָּל־טוּב (kol tuv) is 'every good thing'; the English drops כָּל ('all').

second_reading.note: כָּל־טוּב is 'all good things'; the quantifier כָּל is dropped in the current English.

corrections.proposed_english: houses full of all good things you did not fill, hewn cisterns you did not hew, vineyards and olive groves you did not plant—and you eat and are satisfied,

corrections.hebrew: רַק קָדָשֶׁיךָ אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיוּ לְךָ וּנְדָרֶיךָ תִּשָּׂא וּבָאתָ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר יְהוָה׃
corrections.english: Take your sacred things and your vowed offerings and go to the place YHWH will choose.

first_reading.proposed: But take your sacred things that you have and your vowed offerings and go to the place YHWH will choose.
first_reading.reason: Restrictive רַק ('only/but', the exception to local slaughter) and אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיוּ לְךָ ('that you have') are not rendered.

second_reading.note: Restrictive רַק and the relative clause אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיוּ לְךָ are both unrendered; the verse is an exception to the preceding permission, which 'But' marks.

corrections.proposed_english: But take your sacred things that you have and your vowed offerings and go to the place YHWH will choose.

corrections.hebrew: הַרְנִינוּ גוֹיִם עַמּוֹ כִּי דַם־עֲבָדָיו יִקּוֹם וְנָקָם יָשִׁיב לְצָרָיו וְכִפֶּר אַדְמָתוֹ עַמּוֹ׃
corrections.english: Rejoice, nations, with His people, for He avenges His servants’ blood, repays His adversaries, and makes atonement for His land and people.

first_reading.proposed: Acclaim His people, nations, for He avenges His servants’ blood, repays His adversaries, and makes atonement for His land and people.
first_reading.reason: MT הַרְנִינוּ גוֹיִם עַמּוֹ has no עִם ('with'); עַמּוֹ is the object: 'nations, acclaim His people' (Onkelos, Rashi). 'Rejoice ... with His people' is the Septuagint reading (meta tou laou autou), kept by the KJV.

second_reading.note: הַרְנִינוּ גוֹיִם עַמּוֹ has no עִם; עַמּוֹ is the object (Onkelos, Rashi), and 'with His people' is the Septuagint and KJV reading.

corrections.proposed_english: Acclaim His people, nations, for He avenges His servants’ blood, repays His adversaries, and makes atonement for His land and people.

corrections.hebrew: אָז יְרַד שָׂרִיד לְאַדִּירִים עָם יְהוָה יְרַד־לִי בַּגִּבּוֹרִים׃
corrections.english: Then a remnant went down to the nobles; YHWH’s people went down for me among the warriors.

first_reading.proposed: Then a remnant went down to the nobles of the people; YHWH went down for me among the warriors.
first_reading.reason: MT accents and pausal עָם close the first colon (לְאַדִּירִים עָם); יְהוָה is subject of the second יְרַד. English joins them as 'YHWH's people', the Septuagint's division (λαὸς κυρίου), not the pointed text's.

second_reading.note: Pausal עָם under the atnach ends the first colon and cannot be construct to יְהוָה, which is the subject of the second יְרַד.

corrections.proposed_english: Then a remnant went down to the nobles of the people; YHWH went down for me among the warriors.

corrections.hebrew: וְכָלֵב בֶּן־חֶצְרוֹן הוֹלִיד אֶת־עֲזוּבָה אִשָּׁה וְאֶת־יְרִיעוֹת וְאֵלֶּה בָנֶיהָ יֵשֶׁר וְשׁוֹבָב וְאַרְדּוֹן׃
corrections.english: Caleb son of Hezron fathered Azubah-ishah and Jerioth. These were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.

first_reading.proposed: Caleb son of Hezron fathered children by Azubah his wife and by Jerioth. These were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
first_reading.reason: אִשָּׁה ('wife, woman') is left untranslated and fused into an invented name 'Azubah-ishah', making Azubah Caleb's child; עֲזוּבָה אִשָּׁה is 'Azubah, [his] wife' (cf. 2:19, where she dies and he takes Ephrath).

second_reading.note: אִשָּׁה is 'wife', not part of a name; הוֹלִיד אֶת־עֲזוּבָה אִשָּׁה is 'begot children by Azubah his wife', and בָנֶיהָ are her sons.

corrections.proposed_english: Caleb son of Hezron fathered children by Azubah his wife and by Jerioth. These were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.

corrections.hebrew: וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִים שַׁלּוּם וְעַקּוּב וְטַלְמֹן וַאֲחִימָן וַאֲחִיהֶם שַׁלּוּם הָרֹאשׁ׃
corrections.english: The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers; Shallum was the head.

first_reading.proposed: The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, and Ahiman; their brother Shallum was the head.
first_reading.reason: וַאֲחִיהֶם is pointed singular, 'and their brother', in apposition to Shallum ('their brother Shallum was the head'); the English makes it a plural 'their brothers' added to the list.

second_reading.note: וַאֲחִיהֶם is singular, 'their brother' (plural would be וַאֲחֵיהֶם), in apposition to שַׁלּוּם הָרֹאשׁ; 'their brothers' adds a group the Hebrew lacks.

corrections.proposed_english: The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, and Ahiman; their brother Shallum was the head.

corrections.hebrew: כִּי־גֵרִים אֲנַחְנוּ לְפָנֶיךָ וְתוֹשָׁבִים כְּכָל־אֲבֹתֵינוּ כַּצֵּל יָמֵינוּ עַל־הָאָרֶץ וְאֵין מִקְוֶה׃
corrections.english: We are strangers before You and resident sojourners, like all our fathers. Our days upon the earth are like a shadow, and there is no abiding hope.

first_reading.proposed: We are strangers before You and resident sojourners, like all our fathers. Our days upon the earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope.
first_reading.reason: וְאֵין מִקְוֶה is simply 'and there is no hope'; 'abiding' has no Hebrew counterpart and echoes the KJV's 'none abiding'.

second_reading.note: וְאֵין מִקְוֶה is 'and there is no hope'; 'abiding' has no counterpart and weakens the denial to hope that merely does not last.

corrections.proposed_english: We are strangers before You and resident sojourners, like all our fathers. Our days upon the earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope.

corrections.hebrew: וַיּוֹצֵא יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־שָׂרֵי הַמֵּאוֹת פְּקוּדֵי הַחַיִל וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם הוֹצִיאוּהָ אֶל־מִבֵּית הַשְּׂדֵרוֹת וְהַבָּא אַחֲרֶיהָ יוּמַת בֶּחָרֶב כִּי אָמַר הַכֹּהֵן לֹא תְמִיתוּהָ בֵּית יְהוָה׃
corrections.english: [BHS 23:14] Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds appointed over the force and said to them, “Take her outside the ranks, and anyone following her shall be put to death with the sword.” For the priest had said, “Do not put her to death in YHWH's house.”

first_reading.proposed: [BHS 23:14] Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds appointed over the force and said to them, “Take her out between the ranks, and anyone following her shall be put to death with the sword.” For the priest had said, “Do not put her to death in YHWH's house.”
first_reading.reason: אֶל־מִבֵּית הַשְּׂדֵרוֹת means 'to within/between the ranks' (מִבֵּית = inside); 'outside the ranks' reverses the spatial sense.

second_reading.note: מִבֵּית is the idiom 'inside, within' (cf. מִבֵּית לַפָּרֹכֶת); אֶל־מִבֵּית הַשְּׂדֵרוֹת is 'to within the ranks', so 'outside' reverses it.

corrections.proposed_english: [BHS 23:14] Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds appointed over the force and said to them, “Take her out between the ranks, and anyone following her shall be put to death with the sword.” For the priest had said, “Do not put her to death in YHWH's house.”

corrections.hebrew: ואוצאה [וָאֲצַוֶּה] אוֹתָם עַל־אִדּוֹ הָרֹאשׁ בְּכָסִפְיָא הַמָּקוֹם וָאָשִׂימָה בְּפִיהֶם דְּבָרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל־אִדּוֹ אָחִיו הנתונים [הַנְּתִינִים] בְּכָסִפְיָא הַמָּקוֹם לְהָבִיא־לָנוּ מְשָׁרְתִים לְבֵית אֱלֹהֵינוּ׃
corrections.english: I directed them to Iddo, the head at the place Casiphia, and put words in their mouths to speak to Iddo and his brothers the Nethinim at the place Casiphia, to bring us ministers for the house of our God.

first_reading.proposed: I directed them to Iddo, the head at the place Casiphia, and put words in their mouths to speak to Iddo and his brother, the Nethinim at the place Casiphia, to bring us ministers for the house of our God.
first_reading.reason: MT אֶל־אִדּוֹ אָחִיו is pointed singular, 'Iddo his brother', with no conjunction; English 'and his brothers' is the plural reading of the versions (Vulgate, 1 Esdras) and modern emendation.

second_reading.note: אָחִיו is pointed singular, 'his brother' (plural would be אֶחָיו); 'his brothers' is the reading of the versions, not of the Masoretic pointing.

corrections.proposed_english: I directed them to Iddo, the head at the place Casiphia, and put words in their mouths to speak to Iddo and his brother, the Nethinim at the place Casiphia, to bring us ministers for the house of our God.

corrections.hebrew: לְלֶחֶם הַמַּעֲרֶכֶת וּמִנְחַת הַתָּמִיד וּלְעוֹלַת הַתָּמִיד הַשַּׁבָּתוֹת הֶחֳדָשִׁים לַמּוֹעֲדִים וְלַקֳּדָשִׁים וְלַחַטָּאוֹת לְכַפֵּר עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכֹל מְלֶאכֶת בֵּית־אֱלֹהֵינוּ׃
corrections.english: | conventional 10:33 for the bread arranged before God, the regular grain offering and the regular burnt offering, the Sabbaths, new moons and appointed feasts, the holy offerings and the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.

first_reading.proposed: | conventional 10:33 for the bread of the arrangement, the regular grain offering and the regular burnt offering, the Sabbaths, new moons and appointed feasts, the holy offerings and the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.
first_reading.reason: לֶחֶם הַמַּעֲרֶכֶת is 'the bread of the arrangement/row'; the English adds 'before God', which is not in the Hebrew.

corrections.proposed_english: | conventional 10:33 for the bread of the arrangement, the regular grain offering and the regular burnt offering, the Sabbaths, new moons and appointed feasts, the holy offerings and the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.

corrections.hebrew: אֲשֶׁר קְצִירוֹ רָעֵב יֹאכֵל וְאֶל־מִצִּנִּים יִקָּחֵהוּ וְשָׁאַף צַמִּים חֵילָם׃
corrections.english: The hungry eat his harvest and take it even from among thorns, and the thirsty pant after their wealth.

first_reading.reason: 'the thirsty' reads צְמֵאִים with Aquila, Symmachus, Syriac and Vulgate; MT צַמִּים is 'snare' (so rendered at 18:9) or, with Targum and Rashi, 'robbers'.

second_reading.note: צַמִּים as pointed is not צְמֵאִים 'thirsty', which is the versions' reading; Targum and Rashi take it as 'robbers', which the proposal follows.

corrections.proposed_english: The hungry eat his harvest and take it even from among thorns, and robbers pant after their wealth.

corrections.hebrew: חַטָּאתִי אוֹדִיעֲךָ וַעֲוֺנִי לֹא־כִסִּיתִי אָמַרְתִּי אוֹדֶה עֲלֵי פְשָׁעַי לַיהוָה וְאַתָּה נָשָׂאתָ עֲוֺן חַטָּאתִי סֶלָה׃
corrections.english: I will make my sin known to You; I have not covered my iniquity. I said, “I will confess my rebellions against myself to YHWH,” and You bore away the iniquity of my sin. Selah.

first_reading.proposed: I will make my sin known to You; I have not covered my iniquity. I said, “I will confess my rebellions to YHWH,” and You bore away the iniquity of my sin. Selah.
first_reading.reason: MT עֲלֵי פְשָׁעַי is the poetic preposition 'concerning my rebellions'; 'against myself' reads it as עָלַי, the Septuagint/Vulgate reading (kat' emou, adversum me), which the Hebrew pointing does not give.

second_reading.note: עֲלֵי פְשָׁעַי is poetic עַל, 'concerning my rebellions'; 'against myself' reads עָלַי with the Septuagint and renders the word a second time.

corrections.proposed_english: I will make my sin known to You; I have not covered my iniquity. I said, “I will confess my rebellions to YHWH,” and You bore away the iniquity of my sin. Selah.

corrections.hebrew: אִם־רָאִיתָ גַנָּב וַתִּרֶץ עִמּוֹ וְעִם מְנָאֲפִים חֶלְקֶךָ׃
corrections.english: If you see a thief, you run with him; your portion is with adulterers.

first_reading.proposed: If you see a thief, you are pleased with him; your portion is with adulterers.
first_reading.reason: MT points וַתִּרֶץ, from רצה, 'you are pleased/consent with him'. 'You run with him' renders וַתָּרָץ (from רוץ), the vocalization behind the Septuagint's 'you ran along with him'.

second_reading.note: וַתִּרֶץ is the apocopated imperfect of רָצָה, 'you were pleased, consented' (so Rashi); 'run' needs וַתָּרָץ from רוּץ, the Septuagint's vocalization.

corrections.proposed_english: If you see a thief, you are pleased with him; your portion is with adulterers.

corrections.hebrew: יִמָּאֲסוּ כְמוֹ־מַיִם יִתְהַלְּכוּ־לָמוֹ יִדְרֹךְ חצו [חִצָּיו] כְּמוֹ יִתְמֹלָלוּ׃
corrections.english: Let them be despised; let them walk as through water. He will aim His arrows, so that they are cut down.

first_reading.proposed: Let them be despised; let them go their way like water. He will aim His arrows, so that they are cut down.
first_reading.reason: כְמוֹ־מַיִם יִתְהַלְּכוּ־לָמוֹ is 'like water they go their way' (they themselves are like water running off); 'walk as through water' turns the simile into a medium they walk through.

second_reading.note: כְמוֹ־מַיִם יִתְהַלְּכוּ־לָמוֹ likens them to water that runs off; כְמוֹ is 'like', and nothing in the Hebrew answers to 'through'.

corrections.proposed_english: Let them be despised; let them go their way like water. He will aim His arrows, so that they are cut down.

corrections.hebrew: חַטַּאת־פִּימוֹ דְּבַר־שְׂפָתֵימוֹ וְיִלָּכְדוּ בִגְאוֹנָם וּמֵאָלָה וּמִכַּחַשׁ יְסַפֵּרוּ׃
corrections.english: The sin of their mouth is the word of their lips; the poor are trapped through their arrogance, and through the curse and falsehood they recount.

first_reading.proposed: The sin of their mouth is the word of their lips; let them be trapped through their arrogance, and through the curse and falsehood they recount.
